stories.headline: Strata 0.2.12 roughly triples prompt speed on 12 GB cards with a tuned DFlash2 drafter
stories.summary: Strata 0.2.12 shipped on November 7, 2026. The project's GitHub release, published at 3:54 AM ET, sets the app and Terminal to 0.2.12 and Control and the engine packages to 0.1.58. Release notes say the update adds a tuned DFlash2 drafter and faster prompt processing on NVIDIA, A
stories.body:
Strata 0.2.12 shipped on November 7, 2026. The project's GitHub release, published at 3:54 AM ET, sets the app and Terminal to 0.2.12 and Control and the engine packages to 0.1.58. Release notes say the update adds a tuned DFlash2 drafter and faster prompt processing on NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple hardware. On an RTX 3060 12 GB card running the UD IQ4 XS v31 quant, Strata reports prompt speed rising from 87 to 264 tokens per second at a 2K context and from 361 to 981 tokens per second at 32K. The same notes report prompt gains on Strix Halo Windows machines and both prompt and output gains on an M5 Max, plus a batch of tool call fixes.

That matters because reading a long prompt is usually the slow part of running agents on a local machine, so a claim of about 3 times faster prompt reads on a common 12 GB card is a real change for people who already run models at home. Strata says Auto now picks the tuned DFlash2 drafter on several setups, including Mac for those quants and 12 GB NVIDIA cards on UD IQ4 XS v31, and that the extra drafter file downloads once (about 0.34 GB). Those speed figures are Strata's own measurements against 0.2.11, not an independent benchmark, and the notes also list losses on some JSON and tool call tests.

Robert's AI Companies: Real Estate list carried the news via @dextune. Watch whether those prompt gains show up after the app's updater or the project's update command, and whether later builds change the Radeon default that still prefers MTP.

stories.body: METR published a review of the Risks from automated R&D section of Anthropic's August 2026 Risk Report, done with access to the nonpublic version. The key question was whether Anthropic had crossed its AI R&D acceleration threshold. Anthropic's report said no, and METR's best guess was also no, but METR says the public report understated how plausible it was that acceleration was above the threshold. stories.headline: Researchers find Claude Code can store passwords and API keys that later appear on GitHub
stories.summary: Apiiro researchers found that Claude Code can retain secrets in project settings that later appear in public GitHub repositories, according to Cyber Security News. Choosing "Yes, and don't ask again" can store an approved shell command, including a password or API key embedded in
stories.body:
Apiiro researchers found that Claude Code can retain secrets in project settings that later appear in public GitHub repositories, according to Cyber Security News. Choosing "Yes, and don't ask again" can store an approved shell command, including a password or API key embedded in it, as an allow rule in .claude/settings.local.json. If that file is committed, the secret can become public. @The_Cyber_News carried the report on Robert's Tech News list; this is third party security research, not an Anthropic announcement.

Cyber Security News reports that Apiiro examined 104,185 public copies of the local settings file and found real secrets in 1,122 files, containing 1,379 distinct credentials. Including earlier commits, shared settings and agent transcripts, the researchers reported 2,539 secrets across 1,994 public repositories. Collection ran November 1 through 3, 2026. The report identified 63 affected organizations, mostly software companies, and said one company confirmed that an exposed key had been live. These are Apiiro's findings as reported by Cyber Security News, not an independent audit by this desk.

The report says Claude Code adds a global Git exclude on the machine when it first writes the file, but that protection does not travel with the project, cover files already tracked, or reliably protect a folder later turned into a repository. This makes local agent settings part of the credential handling risk around version control. Watch for an Anthropic product or documentation change and confirmation that exposed credentials have been rotated.
stories.why_it_matters: Robert's Tech News list carried @The_Cyber_News.
